definition: In this psychology context, virtual reality is a computer-generated environment used to create controlled situations that still resemble real-life experience. It is used in stress research to provoke and measure responses under settings that are both standardized and realistic.

reasons: The packet excerpt does not support the claim that virtual reality is a “computer-generated environment.”

While the packet mentions “VR-based stress paradigms” used to “induce stress in controlled yet ecologically valid settings,” it does not explicitly support “used to create controlled situations that still resemble real-life experience.”

The packet does not state that VR is “used in stress research to provoke and measure responses,” nor does it explicitly support the characterization that settings are “both standardized and realistic.”
The packet supports VR stress paradigms, not a general definition of virtual reality as a computer-generated environment, so the opening claim is broader than the source.

“Provoke and measure responses” is only indirectly supported by the source’s description of inducing stress and examining response systems; the definition adds a stronger, more general purpose than the packet states.
